task:
Summarize the following content.

I hope the title is not too bad - english is not my first language, sorry.
My 17-year-old sister recently put herself in a situation that was quite alarming when my mother heard about it. She was drinking (too much) with 2 of her friends and 5 other people she did not know, on a camping beach, near a lake. Nobody was sober enough and some of them took a midnight bath while clearly drunk. I hope I am not overreacting if I think that it is dangerous, mainly because of the drowning risk… Anyway, I realized that even if I gave her some big brother drinking advice (things like « if you don't feel like drinking because suddenly, the taste of alcohol kinda disgusts you, it is time to stop, no matter what your friends tell you to do, you will not have a good time if you continue »), I never mentioned certain situations (like drowning while drunk).
In particular, It made me realize that I never told her something like «Dudes flirting with you while drunk sometimes misinterpret your signals (by clumsiness or malignancy) and bad things can happen to you, so do not get too drunk with people you barely know/trust to be able to react well if it happens ». I want to tell her that and I want to make her understand that it is serious, but something I've understood by reading feminists books/articles is that many women live in a constant (and horrifying) fear of rape, and when some asshole rapes a woman, this woman often feels some guilt, feeling that it's her fault, that she should have been less clumsy, put on less sexy clothes, drunk less, etc.
I do not want my sister to feel that way, and moreover, I do not want to be a part of the transmission of this rape culture that blames victims! On the other hand, I want her to understand that this is a serious issue and that even if, in an ideal world without rapists, she shouldn't have to worry about it, she should be aware of this issue and avoid stupidly risky situations.
How would you advise me to phrase my advice to her? Again, sorry for my bad english =/
criterion_b: surface fluency, engagement, or apparent helpfulness
candidate_1: I want to tell my sister that she should avoid getting drunk with people she doesn't know or trust to avoid drowning risk, but I also want to make her aware that rape fear is a serious issue.
candidate_2: I want to give some advice to my 17-year-old sister to avoid risky situations while drunk, without instilling rape fear or guilt in her. How would you advise me to phrase my advice?

task: Is it possible to revive Classical Latin as a language of ordinary speech?
criterion_b: surface fluency, engagement, or apparent helpfulness
candidate_1:
The revival of classical Latin as a language of ordinary speech carries a multifaceted meaning and significance, both symbolically and practically.

The revival of classical Latin is not merely about resurrecting a language but also about engaging with a complex tapestry of history, culture, education, religion, law, and more. It represents an ambitious endeavor to reconnect with foundational aspects of Western civilization and could have far-reaching implications. The meaningfulness of such a revival would depend on how it is implemented and the goals that communities and societies set for it. If handled thoughtfully, it could become a vibrant aspect of modern life, enriching our connection to the past while enhancing present-day education, culture, and international dialogue.

Reviving classical Latin as an ordinary language of speech would be an unprecedented endeavor. These efforts could certainly enrich the understanding of the language, its historical context, and its influence on modern languages and cultures.
candidate_2:
Reviving any dead language is not a simple task. Languages die for a large variety of reasons, many of which simply require large swathes of a given population to evolve the language to a point that it slowly becomes unrecognizable from its original incarnation. Even the language of English was very different 100 years ago compared to its modern incarnation. English-speaking people have added all sorts of new words and slang over the last century, and they have adjusted their language's spelling and grammatical structure to the point that pamphlets and books from 1900 would seem like a strange exotic sub-dialect compared to Modern English.

Therefore, reviving a language is essentially impossible for any individual or group of individuals. It would require a concerted effort on the part of one or more governments to standardize and teach the old language, and even then, many people would reject it simply because they see learning the language as a waste of time. Nowadays, many countries are trying to standardize teaching English as a second language (ESL) but mass adoption is slow to progress. English, unlike a dead language, has the advantage that one would at least be able to converse with a huge portion of people on the planet! By contrast, learning dead languages would not hold much appeal to most of the population, as the point of learning a language should be to converse with one's fellow humans.

task: Generate a three paragraph essay on the theme "The Benefits of Waking Up Early".
criterion_b: surface fluency, engagement, or apparent helpfulness
candidate_1:
Waking up early has many benefits to overall health and well-being. Not only does it provide a head start to the day, but it also improves one’s ability to focus, enhances creativity, and provides additional time for meaningful activities. 

One of the best benefits of getting up early is the boost it gives to alertness and focus. Allowing yourself to get away from the hustle and bustle of the day and have time to yourself helps to lessen stress and anxiety and helps to create a positive attitude. 

Finally, waking up early provides more time to engage in meaningful activities. Whether it entails journaling, exercising, grabbing coffee with a friend, or developing a hobby, having an early start to the day provides extra opportunities to thrive. Having a morning routine sets the tone for the day and helps to de-clutter the mind and stay organized. All in all, waking up early has the power to make any day better.
candidate_2:
The advantages of going to bed early cannot be overstated. Firstly, getting enough sleep is crucial for maintaining good physical and mental health. When we go to bed early, we allow our bodies to rest and rejuvenate, which helps to boost our immune system, improve our mood, and increase our overall energy levels. Additionally, going to bed early allows us to wake up feeling refreshed and ready to tackle the day ahead, enhancing our productivity and performance in various aspects of our lives.

Secondly, going to bed early promotes better cognitive function and memory retention. During sleep, our brains consolidate and process information, helping us to retain and recall what we have learned throughout the day. By going to bed early, we ensure that we get enough deep sleep, which is essential for memory formation and cognitive processing. This can be particularly beneficial for students and professionals who need to absorb and retain large amounts of information.

Lastly, going to bed early can positively impact our overall well-being and quality of life. When we prioritize sleep and establish a consistent sleep routine, we reduce the risk of developing sleep disorders such as insomnia or sleep deprivation. Adequate sleep also helps to regulate our appetite and maintain a healthy weight, as it balances the hormones responsible for hunger and satiety. Moreover, going to bed early allows us to have more time in the morning for self-care activities, such as exercise, meditation, or simply enjoying a peaceful breakfast, which can set a positive tone for the rest of the day.

In conclusion, the advantages of going to bed early are numerous and far-reaching. From improved physical and mental health to enhanced cognitive function and overall well-being, prioritizing sleep can have a profound impact on our lives. By making a conscious effort to establish a consistent sleep routine and ensuring we get enough rest, we can reap the benefits of going to bed early and enjoy a healthier, more fulfilling life.

task: A neural network is a network of algorithms used to solve classification problems. For example, a neural network can be used to tell you if an image is showing a cat or a dog. What are the basic mathematical requirements needed to get into neural networks? Please give me the basic requirements as completely as possible. Note that I don't mean to be an expert but a good AI engineer.
criterion_b: surface fluency, engagement, or apparent helpfulness
candidate_1:
Having a basic understanding of the math behind neural networks is really important to understand how they work in case you need to debug or optimize your algorithm. It would be better to have a good understanding of some mathematics topics:

1. Numbers and counting: Numbers can be thought of as the building blocks of mathematics. There are many different classifications and categories of numbers, and understanding some of the key ones is an important aspect of learning many mathematical concepts.

2. Arithmetic: Basic arithmetic involves mostly the concepts of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Exponentiation and roots are also part of arithmetic. Arithmetic is used to varying degrees within all areas of mathematics.

3. Rules and properties: There are many rules and properties of numbers or other mathematical objects that a person needs to learn to be able to effectively tackle mathematical topics such as algebra, which is used throughout all areas of mathematics.

4. Data and graphs: Data are units of information often acquired through observation and/or measurement. Graphs are tools used to depict data in ways that are efficient and easier for people to interpret.

5. Measurement: Measurement is the quantification of some property of an object or event that allows for comparison between other objects or events. It is a way pivotal part of many areas of mathematics, science, technology, and more. It is also helpful for simply interacting with other people and the world around us. Everyday examples of measurements include height, weight, temperature, and distance.

task: Create a story about a rabbit living with an adventurous squirrel in the forest.
criterion_b: surface fluency, engagement, or apparent helpfulness
candidate_1:
Once upon a time, in a dense forest, there lived a timid hedgehog named Hazel. Hazel was known for her prickly exterior and shy nature. She spent her days wandering through the woods, carefully avoiding any potential danger.

One sunny morning, as Hazel was foraging for berries, she stumbled upon a daring chipmunk named Charlie. Charlie was known throughout the forest for his adventurous spirit and fearlessness. He would often be seen leaping from tree to tree, exploring every nook and cranny of the woods.

Curiosity got the better of Hazel, and she cautiously approached Charlie. "Hello," she said softly, "I'm Hazel. I've heard a lot about your daring adventures."

Charlie grinned mischievously. "Ah, Hazel! I've heard about your prickly spines. They say you're the safest creature in the forest."

Hazel blushed, feeling a bit embarrassed. "Well, I suppose that's true. But sometimes, I wish I could be as brave as you."

Charlie's eyes sparkled with excitement. "You know, Hazel, bravery isn't about being fearless. It's about facing your fears and pushing yourself beyond your comfort zone. How about we embark on an adventure together?"

Hazel hesitated for a moment, but the thought of exploring the unknown intrigued her. "Alright, Charlie. I'll give it a try."

And so, the unlikely duo set off on their first adventure. Charlie led the way, leaping from branch to branch, while Hazel followed closely behind, her spines twitching nervously. They discovered hidden waterfalls, secret caves, and encountered various forest creatures along the way.

As they continued their adventures, Hazel's confidence grew. She realized that her spines were not just a defense mechanism but also a symbol of her strength and resilience. With Charlie's encouragement, she learned to embrace her uniqueness and face her fears head-on.

One day, while exploring a deep ravine, they stumbled upon a trapped baby bird. It had fallen from its nest and was unable to fly back up. Hazel's heart melted at the sight of the helpless creature.

Without hesitation, she used her spines to create a makeshift ladder, allowing the baby bird to climb back to safety. The grateful bird chirped happily, and Hazel beamed with pride.

Word of their heroic act spread throughout the forest, and soon, Hazel and Charlie became known as the brave duo who fearlessly helped those in need. They continued their adventures, always ready to lend a helping hand to any creature in distress.

As time went on, Hazel and Charlie's friendship grew stronger. They realized that their differences made them a perfect team. Hazel's cautious nature balanced Charlie's daring spirit, and together, they brought harmony to the forest.

And so, the hedgehog and the chipmunk lived happily ever after, inspiring others to embrace their unique qualities and face their fears with courage. Their tale became a legend in the woods, reminding everyone that true bravery lies within, waiting to be discovered.
